Meta-Analysis Tables

Source: vignettes/articles/meta-analysis.qmd 
library(apa7)
library(metafor)
library(dplyr)

apa_parameters and apa_performance make APA-style tables of meta-analyses fit with metafor::rma:

Table Function Contents
Studies and pooled estimate apa_parameters Each study’s effect size, confidence interval, and weight, followed by the pooled estimate
Meta-regression apa_parameters Coefficients of the moderators, as for other regression models
Heterogeneity apa_performance k, Q, τ2, I2, and, for meta-regressions, the test of the moderators and R2
Subgroups apa_subgroups Each subgroup’s pooled estimate and the test of subgroup differences
Publication bias apa_publication_bias Egger’s regression test, the rank correlation test, and trim and fill, with adjusted estimates

Studies and the Pooled Estimate

The dat.molloy2014 data set in the metadat package (installed with metafor) has the correlations between conscientiousness and medication adherence in 16 studies. Correlations are meta-analyzed as Fisher’s z values (measure = "ZCOR" in escalc), and slab gives the study labels:

d_adherence <- escalc(
  measure = "ZCOR",
  ri = ri,
  ni = ni,
  data = metadat::dat.molloy2014,
  slab = paste(authors, year)
)

fit_adherence <- rma(yi, vi, data = d_adherence)

apa_parameters(fit_adherence) |>
  apa_flextable(note = TRUE)

Note. Effect sizes are correlations, analyzed on the Fisher’s z scale and converted back for the table. The 16 studies were pooled with a random-effects model, with τ2 estimated by restricted maximum likelihood. Weights are percentages of the total weight. Test of the pooled estimate: z = 4.75, p < .001; 95% PI [−.04, .32]. Heterogeneity: Q(15) = 38.16, p < .001, τ2 = 0.01, I2 = 61.7%. CI = confidence interval; PI = prediction interval.

Each study’s correlation and confidence interval, and the pooled estimate below the rule, are converted back from Fisher’s z to r. The weights are each study’s percentage of the total weight in the random-effects model. The note names the measure and the model, and it gives the test of the pooled estimate, its 95% prediction interval (the range in which the true effect of a new study is expected to fall), and the test of heterogeneity.

The column of effect sizes is named by the measure given to escalc: for example, g for standardized mean differences ("SMD"), r for correlations ("COR" or "ZCOR"), and OR, RR, or IRR for odds ratios, risk ratios, and incidence rate ratios. Ratios are analyzed on the log scale and exponentiated for the table. With transform = FALSE, estimates stay on the scale on which they were analyzed (e.g., log risk ratios). With weights = FALSE, the weights are left out.

Heterogeneity

apa_performance gives the heterogeneity statistics:

apa_performance(fit_adherence) |>
  apa_flextable(note = TRUE)

k

Q(15)

p

τ2

I2 (%)

16

38.16

<.001

0.01

Note. τ2 was estimated by restricted maximum likelihood. k = number of studies; Q = test of heterogeneity; τ2 = variance of the true effects; I2 = percentage of total variability due to heterogeneity.

With metrics = "all", the table adds τ, H2, and confidence intervals of τ2 and I2.

Ratio Measures

In the dat.bcg data set, 13 trials compared the risk of tuberculosis in people who were and were not vaccinated with BCG. The effect sizes are risk ratios, which are analyzed on the log scale and exponentiated for the table:

d_bcg <- escalc(
  measure = "RR",
  ai = tpos, bi = tneg, ci = cpos, di = cneg,
  data = metadat::dat.bcg,
  slab = paste(author, year)
) |> 
  rename(Latitude = ablat,
         Allocation = alloc) |> 
  mutate(Allocation = factor(stringr::str_to_title(Allocation)))


fit_bcg <- rma(yi, vi, data = d_bcg)

apa_parameters(fit_bcg) |>
  apa_flextable(note = TRUE)

Meta-Regression

Moderators are added with mods. The vaccine appeared to work better in trials farther from the equator, so here the absolute latitude of each trial is a moderator:

fit_latitude <- rma(yi, vi, mods = ~ Latitude, data = d_bcg)

apa_parameters(fit_latitude) |>
  apa_flextable(note = TRUE)

Note. τ2 was estimated by restricted maximum likelihood. k = number of studies; QE = test of residual heterogeneity; τ2 = variance of the true effects; I2 = percentage of total variability due to heterogeneity; QM = omnibus test of the moderators; R2 = percentage of heterogeneity explained by the moderators.

For a meta-regression, apa_parameters shows the intercept and moderators, as for other regression models. Coefficients (B) are on the scale on which the effect sizes were analyzed (here, log risk ratios), and for ratio measures, the exponentiated coefficients are added (here, RR): each degree of latitude multiplies the risk ratio by about 0.97. apa_performance adds the omnibus test of the moderators (QM) and the percentage of heterogeneity they explain (R2), and QE is the test of the heterogeneity that remains.

Subgroup Analysis

A subgroup analysis compares the pooled estimates of groups of studies. In the BCG trials, participants were assigned to the vaccine at random, alternately, or systematically. apa_subgroups pools each group of trials and compares them:

apa_subgroups(fit_bcg, Allocation) |>
  apa_flextable(note = TRUE)

Note. Effect sizes are risk ratios, analyzed on the log scale and exponentiated for the table. Each subgroup of Allocation was pooled with its own random-effects model, with τ2 estimated by restricted maximum likelihood. The overall estimate is from the meta-analysis of all effect sizes. Test of subgroup differences (Borenstein et al., 2009): Qbetween(2) = 1.86, p = .39. k = number of studies; CI = confidence interval; I2 = percentage of total variability due to heterogeneity.

By default, each subgroup has its own τ2, and the subgroups are compared with Qbetween, the heterogeneity of the subgroup estimates. With tau2 = "common", the subgroups share one τ2, which is estimated more precisely when subgroups have few studies: the estimates come from a meta-regression with the subgroup as a categorical moderator, and the subgroups are compared with its omnibus test (QM). The subgroup variable can be a column of the data (quoted or unquoted) or a vector (e.g., d_bcg$Latititude > 30).

Publication Bias

apa_publication_bias tests for publication bias (small-study effects) and gives estimates adjusted for it, as computed by metafor: Egger’s regression test, with its limit estimate (the predicted effect of a study with a standard error of zero); Begg and Mazumdar’s rank correlation test; and trim and fill, with the number of studies it imputed (k0) and the pooled estimate with them included:

apa_publication_bias(fit_adherence) |>
  apa_flextable(note = TRUE)

Method

Statistic

2  

.13

[ .06, .19]

Note. The unadjusted pooled estimate of the 16 studies is r = .15, 95% CI [.09, .21]. Egger’s regression test (Egger et al., 1997) is the test of the standard error in a meta-regression of the effect sizes on their standard errors; its adjusted estimate is the predicted effect as the standard error approaches zero. The rank correlation test (Begg & Mazumdar, 1994) is Kendall’s τ between the standardized effect sizes and their sampling variances. Trim and fill (Duval & Tweedie, 2000) with the L0 estimator imputed 2 studies on the left side of the funnel plot; its adjusted estimate includes them. Estimates are correlations, converted from the scale on which they were analyzed. CI = confidence interval; k0 = number of imputed studies.

The adjusted estimates are on the same scale as the table of studies (here, correlations), and the note gives the unadjusted pooled estimate for comparison. Add "fsn" to methods for the fail-safe N, which is widely criticized and is not shown by default. These methods are available for rma models without moderators.

Multilevel Meta-Analysis

When studies report several effect sizes, the effect sizes are not independent, and a multilevel (three-level) model with rma.mv has a random intercept for each level. In the dat.konstantopoulos2011 data set, 56 schools in 11 school districts compared the achievement of students on modified and traditional school calendars (standardized mean differences). The table of a multilevel model has a row for each effect size, so this example shows only the pooled estimate (studies = FALSE):

fit_schools <- rma.mv(
  yi, vi,
  random = ~ 1 | district / school,
  data = metadat::dat.konstantopoulos2011
)

apa_parameters(fit_schools, studies = FALSE) |>
  apa_flextable(note = TRUE)

The 56 effect sizes were pooled with a multilevel random-effects model with random intercepts for district (11 levels) and school in district (56 levels), with variance components estimated by restricted maximum likelihood. CI = confidence interval.

Note. Variance components were estimated by restricted maximum likelihood. I2 is the multilevel I2 (Cheung, 2014): the percentage of total variability due to heterogeneity at all levels, or at the level in the subscript. k = number of effect sizes; Q = test of heterogeneity; σ2 = variance of the true effects at the level in the subscript.

apa_performance gives the variance of the true effects at each level (σ2, with the level as a subscript) and the multilevel I2 (Cheung, 2014), the percentage of the total variability due to heterogeneity at all levels. With metrics = "all", the table adds σ and confidence intervals of σ2 for each level, and I2 for each level. Meta-regressions of multilevel models work as for rma. Random effects with an ~ inner | outer structure (e.g., correlated outcomes within studies) are not yet supported.

Citations in Notes

Some notes cite the articles that describe a method (e.g., trim and fill and the multilevel I2). In the console and in this article, the citations are written as text. To have them formatted and added to the reference list of a Quarto or R Markdown document, see Citations in notes in the regression article.

Options

  • method = "EE" in rma fits an equal-effects model; the table labels the pooled estimate accordingly, and there is no prediction interval or τ2.
  • test = "knha" in rma uses the Knapp–Hartung adjustment; the pooled estimate is tested with t, and the note says so.
  • studies = FALSE shows only the pooled estimate, with its test, instead of the study rows.
  • Multilevel models with random intercepts (rma.mv with random = ~ 1 | study / effect) are supported; random effects with an ~ inner | outer structure are not yet supported.
